title: A few weeks into AI-assisted gamedev: my 2D MMORPG
author: AkiraVero
selftext:
Hey everyone! I started learning gamedev with AI a few weeks ago and it's turned into a 2D MMORPG — a Ragnarok Online / FFXI / Nostale / Trickster Online type of game which will eventually have content such as  instanced dungeons, open world, PvP, leaderboards, etc. I've basically stopped playing games — building this is more fun.

I went backend-first. I developed an "AI company" — parallel AI engineers, artists, and managers. All state lives in docs the AI reads, so fresh sessions cold-start with full context and pick up mid-task. Pipelines are almost fully autonomous, so down the line I can pump out content really quickly.

Infra: authoritative multiplayer server, channel-based world that shards horizontally (\~1–2k players, path to 5k), plus a custom web DevKit with an asset pipeline and zone editor.

  
I've taken a lot of inspiration from some of the videos / ideas you guys have posted in this channel in the past few weeks!

Video attached, a few screenshots in the comments. What do you guys think?

replies.body: What’s the advantage to it over using some other engine or existing editor?

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: It has a fully API driven back-end which my AI's built out, document and continue to improve with iteration. So they know exactly where to go and how to do it. They execute the workflow, I do the fine tuning and polishing.

comments.author: Jan49_
comments.body: I would suggest more prominent shadows. It would ground the objects more and instantly boost the looks

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: 100% Agreed. Thank you. One of the things on my to-do list is to tackle how to handle shadows and handling them correctly depending on the image. I feel like right now the in-game look is very floaty and theres no real "substance" to it!

comments.author: Shoopbadoopp
comments.body: Can you show or explain more about your art pipeline? I’m experienced in 3D game dev, but am trying to make a 2.5D game using 2D sprites. How are you creating your art assets and getting them to render so well?

replies.author: heavyc-dev
replies.body: I’m doing full 3d but I’m using Claude to run blender in headless mode to do my animating and rigging on meshes. Might be worth a look for you. Kinda depends on what approach you’re doing with 2.5D on if that’s useful for you though

comments.author: Unfair-Frosting-4934
comments.body:
Is this playable in browser? 

  
We'd love to include it on SLAGDOCK, a game portal website similar to miniclip, newgrounds, kongregate.

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body:
It's fully playable in a browser and works great on Ipad and eventually mobile phones (I have not looked into customizing the UI at all to fit into it). I do have it currently hosted online, but it's very basic right now. The showcase is just one zone and a few monster and a few assets. Almost my entire development time has been getting a solid back-end infrastructure with tools to help me develop the game.

  
In the future once I have more systems added and it actually becomes "Playable" I'm hoping to introduce it to everybody and if anyone is interested in the progress / following along have a discord server =).

replies.author: Unfair-Frosting-4934
replies.body: If your link is embed able we can include it on the game portal just lmk

comments.author: Straight-Tea-8564
comments.body: Muito legal, estou fazendo um jogo muito parecido, o que você tem usado para o multiplayer ?

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: Hey! I had responded to your thread recently. I took a lot of inspiration from your game! Sorry I don't speak your language but (AI translation!) - Acho que a nossa stack é parecida, mas as técnicas talvez não: uso Colyseus (Node/TS) com servidor autoritativo e mundo baseado em canais — cada canal roda como instância própria e escala horizontalmente, com sharding entre processos. Cliente em Phaser, contratos TypeScript compartilhados entre cliente e servidor. Boa sorte com o seu!

comments.author: DulaLipa
comments.body:
Why is she committing a genocide on the slimes? 
They don't seem to be doing anything to her, i see her health bar drops a bit but my god, they're merely trying to defend themselves from a one shotting maniac.

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: Don't worry. The slimes WILL HAVE THEIR REVENGE! One of the plans is to implement a quest in the starter zone where you kill a few slimes of each type which spawns a Huge (and cute) KING SLIME that kills you, to teach you how the death mechanic works!

comments.author: heavyc-dev
comments.body: I’m not trying to be rude but the whole “AI company” thing and things being “fully autonomous” is a bad thing not good if your end goal is an actual fun game or fully working product. I’ve never once seen any product not be complete slop that’s made by the larpers with these type of workflows

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: I understand where your coming from. And the goal is not for the design to be autonomous. The goal is for the repeating work and pipelines to be autonomous. The design / goal / end-state is purely coming from me. The implementation on how to achieve that and have throughput to make it something obtainable as a solo-dev is what that is going to achieve. When I say "AI Company" I mean it's a fully self-sustained platform where work can be given from me (as the designer) and passed down along a chain of executives, orchestrators, managers to AI Engineers and implementers. Does that make more sense?

replies.author: heavyc-dev
replies.body: I get you but I imagine “design” is “we need 4 new swords” and letting it take the wheel. The amount of benefit you get from this autonomy is removed if the “design” is actual design

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: That's not correct because my pipelines know exactly what prompt style to take if I say "we need 4 new swords". It has recipes for exactly the style of image generation it needs to do. And as a designer I would not say "we need 4 new swords". I would say something along the lines of "I need a red dragon sword X in length with Y addon's". It knows the base recipe, it's not expected to know the design.

replies.author: heavyc-dev
replies.body: Yes you have a prompt prefix

replies.author: AkiraVero
replies.body: Much more then just that, but yes I do!

replies.author: VerminousSkum
replies.body: its so lame people vibe downvote you for being critical.. lmao then they wake up in 3 months and realized they were getting farmed.

replies.author: heavyc-dev
replies.body: It’s all good I really don’t care about downvotes but yeah it is kind of annoying. I’m very pro AI usage but I just think some practices are kind of nonsense and produce poor output in AIs current state. I see these same type of workflows for non video game coding and they’re always horrendous. It’s more playing “coding simulator” than accomplishing anything meaningful imo
